name: Furlo and Rublo and Game
description: Furlo and Rublo play a game. The table has n piles of coins lying on it, the i -th pile has a i coins. Furlo and Rublo move in turns, Furlo moves first. In one move you are allowed to: choose some pile, let's denote the current number of coins in it as x ; choose some integer y (0 ≤ y < x ; x 1 / 4 ≤ y ≤ x 1 / 2 ) and decrease the number of coins in this pile to y . In other words, after the described move the pile will have y coins left. The player who can't make a move, loses. Your task is to find out, who wins in the given game if both Furlo and Rublo play optimally well.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 77777) — the number of piles. The next line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (1 ≤ a i ≤ 777777777777) — the sizes of piles. The numbers are separated by single spaces. Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin , cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output_specification: If both players play optimally well and Furlo wins, print " Furlo ", otherwise print " Rublo ". Print the answers without the quotes.
subsubtopic: 472. Grundy Number and Basic Game Theory
approach_summary: Compute Sprague-Grundy values g(u) = mex({g(v) : u -> v}). Game state is winning iff XOR sum of independent game components is non-zero.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 255E — Furlo and Rublo and Game [472. Grundy Number and Basic Game Theory]
topic_editorial.summary: Impartial game theory via Sprague-Grundy theorem.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any finite, impartial game under normal play convention is equivalent to a one-pile game of Nim with pile size equal to its Grundy value $g(u) = \text{mex}(\{g(v) : u \to v\})$. A compound game of independent subgames is winning for the first player if and only if $\bigoplus_{i} g_i \ne 0$.
